summary: Vilhelm Peter Grønbech worked in religious studies and linguistics. He earned his cand.mag. at the University of Copenhagen, studying under Vilhelm Thomsen, Karl Verner, and Holger Pedersen. He held docent posts at Copenhagen (1908, 1911) and taught at Danmarks Lærerhøjskole (1912–1919).

Vilhelm Thomsen was a linguist and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Johan Nicolai Madvig and Niels Ludvig Westergaard, later serving there as Privatdozent (1869, 1875) and Professor (1887–1913).

Vilhelm Trenckner worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Johan Nicolai Madvig, Christian Thorning Engelstoft Hermansen, and Niels Ludvig Westergaard. In 1860, he served as a teacher at Det Kgl. Vajsenhus.

Ville Husgafvel is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki (2015–2023) and SOAS University of London (2017–2018), later working as a project researcher at the University of Helsinki (2022–2023).

Vimla Karnatak is a scholar in Indology and philosophy who studied under Gajanan Shastri Musalgaonkar. She served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit at Banaras Hindu University (attested 2000).

Vinay Lal is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Johns Hopkins University (~1982–1984) and was appointed Professor in the Department of History and Asian American Studies at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1993).

Vinaya Kshirsagar specializes in Indology and linguistics. She served as a professor at Dr. D. Y. Patil Medical College, Hospital & Research Centre in 2015 and as Professor-Editor for the Sanskrit Dictionary at Deccan College (attested 2026).

Vincenc Lesný worked in Indology, Buddhist, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Charles University, Oxford, and Bonn under Josef Zubatý, Moriz Winternitz, Arthur Anthony Macdonell, and Hermann Jacobi. He served as Privatdozent (1918) and Professor (1924) at Charles University.

Vincenc Pořízka was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Palacký University Olomouc and Charles University under Vincenc Lesný and Otakar Pertold. He taught at Charles University as Professor of Hindi (1951) and at Humboldt University of Berlin (1960–1967).

Vincent Arthur Smith worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Trinity College Dublin and Cambridge, he served in the Indian Civil Service (1871–1900), as Reader at Dublin (1902–1903) and Oxford (1910), and as Curator of the Indian Institute (~1910–1920).

Vincent Breugem specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He earned his MA and PhD at Leiden University, studied under Lucia Dolce, and attended Taisho, Kyoto, and Hanazono Universities. He was a research fellow at Leiden University (attested 2012).

Vincent Eltschinger specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Fribourg, Lausanne (PhD under Tom Tillemans), and Vienna. He was a research fellow and interim director at IKGA and became Directeur d’études at EPHE (~2015).

Vincent Goossaert is a scholar of sinology and religious studies who studied under Kristofer Schipper (~1993–1997). He worked at CNRS (~1998–2012) and became Professor of Daoist History at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2012).

Vincent Lefèvre specializes in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the École Nationale des Chartes and Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Bruno Dagens, and has served as a curator at the Guimet Museum.

Vincent Tournier specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at EPHE and Leiden under Cristina Scherrer-Schaub and Seishi Karashima. His posts include Maître de conférences at Sciences Po Grenoble and roles at EFEO, Göttingen Academy, and the University of Tokyo.

Vincenz Scherzl was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Charles University, King's College London, Saint Petersburg under Kaetan Kossovich, and Moscow State University. He served as professor of comparative linguistics at the University of Kharkiv (1880–1885) and Odesa University (1885–1906).
Vincenzo Vergiani is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Raffaele Torella. In 2007, he became Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Cambridge.
Vinit Deo is a scholar of Indology, history, archaeology, and philosophy. He earned an external MA in Indology from Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (2022–2024).

Vinod Kumar Roy is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Patna University, the University of Delhi (BA and PhD), and Magadh University, where he became Assistant Professor (Senior Scale) in 2019.

Vinod Mishra is an Indologist and historian. He earned an M.Sc. from Kurukshetra University (1989–1991) and a Ph.D. from Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya (1994–1998), becoming a Professor at Sant Longowal Institute of Engineering and Technology in 2010.
